# Humira Patent Expiry in the U.S.: 2016, 2023, and 2034 Explained


September 25, 2026


&AI Team


Humira's U.S. patent story is easy to flatten into one date. That shortcut obscures three different events: the end of one patent term, contractual entry under settlement/license agreements, and later dates attached to other patents. For patent and competitive-intelligence work, those dates need to stay separate because each answers a different legal or commercial question.


## The short answer


**Humira's basic U.S. adalimumab patent expired at the end of 2016. But U.S. biosimilar competition did not begin until 2023, after settlement/license agreements set contractual entry dates. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration's sponsor-provided[Purple Book list](https://purplebooksearch.fda.gov/patent-list) also contains later patents with dates through 2034.**


Those statements can all be true because a patent expiry, an FDA approval, a settlement license, and a commercial launch are separate events. The Seventh Circuit identified US 6,090,382 as the basic patent and said it[expired at the end of 2016](https://media.ca7.uscourts.gov/cgi-bin/rssExec.pl?Path=Y2022%2FD08-01%2FC%3A20-2402%3AJ%3AEasterbrook%3Aaut%3AT%3AfnOp%3AN%3A2911279%3AS%3A0&Submit=Display) . The U.S. Patent and Trademark Office's (USPTO)[original patent-term-extension certificate](https://www.uspto.gov/sites/default/files/web/offices/pac/dapp/opla/term/certs/6090382.pdf) extended the term by 326 days from February 9, 2016, yielding December 31, 2016. Amgen announced the first U.S. biosimilar availability on[January 31, 2023](https://www.amgen.com/newsroom/press-releases/2023/01/amjevita-adalimumabatto-first-biosimilar-to-humira-now-available-in-the-united-states) . The Purple Book list includes an individual patent date as late as November 14, 2034.


## Humira's U.S. timeline at a glance


Date Event What the date means


December 31, 2002 FDA approved Humira under biologics license application (BLA) 125057 The[original approval](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2002/adalabb123102L.htm) established the reference biologic. It was not a patent-expiry date.


September 23, 2016[FDA approved Amjevita](https://purplebooksearch.fda.gov/index.cfm?blaNo=761024&event=productdetails) The first Humira-reference biosimilar had regulatory approval. It had not launched in the United States.


December 31, 2016 Basic patent US 6,090,382 expired One core patent term ended. Other patents and patent disputes remained.


2017 to 2019 AbbVie and biosimilar manufacturers entered settlement/license agreements The portfolio of agreements set contractual U.S. entry dates in 2023. Some resolved filed litigation, as the[Seventh Circuit later summarized](https://media.ca7.uscourts.gov/cgi-bin/rssExec.pl?Path=Y2022%2FD08-01%2FC%3A20-2402%3AJ%3AEasterbrook%3Aaut%3AT%3AfnOp%3AN%3A2911279%3AS%3A0&Submit=Display) .


January 31, 2023 Amjevita launched in the United States This was the first documented U.S. commercial entry of a Humira biosimilar.


July 1 to 3, 2023 The main biosimilar launch wave followed Several manufacturers announced U.S. availability on product-specific dates.


November 14, 2034 Latest date in the analyzed sponsor-provided Purple Book list This is the descriptive maximum for an individual listed patent, US 9,550,826. It is not a Humira-wide exclusivity date.


The dates describe different events. Sources: Seventh Circuit, FDA Purple Book, FDA biosimilar records, and manufacturer launch notices.


*Sources: Seventh Circuit, FDA Purple Book patent list and biosimilar records, AbbVie's September 28, 2017 announcement, and manufacturer launch notices. The listed dates are sponsor-provided for FDA publication and are not FDA findings of patent validity, enforceability, infringement, applicability, or other legal effect.*


## Why Humira has no single patent-expiry date


The phrase **Humira patent expiration** suggests a single endpoint. A biologic can sit inside several layers of patent protection. The basic Humira patent covered human antibodies that bind tumor necrosis factor alpha (TNF). Later patents addressed subjects such as purified compositions, formulations, dose regimens, treatment methods, manufacturing processes, and injection devices. Each patent has its own claims, prosecution history, term, and potential relationship to a particular biosimilar.


The legal pathway adds another layer. Humira is a biologic governed by the Biologics Price Competition and Innovation Act (BPCIA). It does not follow the small-molecule Hatch-Waxman and[Paragraph IV notice process](https://www.tryandai.com/blog/paragraph-iv-notice-letter) . The Seventh Circuit explained that BPCIA patent litigation does not itself impose the automatic sales stay associated with Hatch-Waxman. An approved biosimilar could launch at risk, though the court recorded that the potential Humira competitors did not do so.


The court's reference to 132 additional Humira-related patents and the 66 patents in the analyzed dataset also measure different universes. The former describes the broader portfolio discussed in the antitrust record. The latter is the set AbbVie provided to FDA for publication under the Purple Book patent-listing provisions.


## What the sponsor-listed portfolio contains


The[Purple Book Patent List](https://purplebooksearch.fda.gov/patent-list) page version displayed as updated June 11, 2025 contains **66 Humira patent rows** for BLA 125057. We grouped those rows conservatively into **21 Google Patents family groups** and assigned practical subject categories from the retained patent titles.


Category Family groups FDA-listed patents Examples of covered subject matter


Manufacturing 10 26 Cell culture, purification, glycosylation, protein heterogeneity, acidic species


Dosing 3 12 Anti-TNF administration and disease-specific dose regimens


Other follow-on uses 3 10 Psoriatic arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, and related treatment methods


Composition 1 11 Purified antibody compositions


Formulation 2 4 Protein and anti-TNF antibody formulations


Device 2 3 Autoinjector and needle-shield mechanisms


**Total** **21** **66**


The grouping is a research aid. A Google family ID is not an official U.S. Patent and Trademark Office family determination, and a family does not have one legal expiration date. The dataset preserves the sponsor-provided date for each patent. Its group-level latest date is only a descriptive maximum.


US 6,090,382 appears as a separate historical-core addendum. It is outside the 66-row Purple Book universe. The[full patent-family CSV](https://www.tryandai.com/blog-media/humira-patent-expiry-landscape/humira-patent-families.csv) includes the patent numbers, applications, dates, category basis, Google Patents grouping keys, and source links. Our guide to[patent-family graphs](https://www.tryandai.com/blog/building-patent-family-graphs-from-imperfect-data) explains why continuity and family relationships need more than matching titles.


## Why U.S. biosimilars arrived in 2023


The 2016 basic-patent expiry did not resolve the later patent disputes. Amgen received FDA approval for Amjevita on September 23, 2016. AbbVie's[September 28, 2017 resolution announcement](https://news.abbvie.com/2017-09-28-AbbVie-Announces-Global-Resolution-of-HUMIRA-R-adalimumab-Patent-Disputes-with-Amgen) said the parties would dismiss their pending litigation and that Amgen's nonexclusive U.S. license would begin January 31, 2023. Amgen announced U.S. availability on that same date.


Other manufacturers entered settlement/license agreements with their own public terms. Some resolved filed litigation; the broader group should not be treated as nine adjudicated lawsuits. Publicly announced entry dates differed. The Seventh Circuit summarized the result: the agreements permitted U.S. entry during 2023 even though some patents had later terms.


The agreements drew antitrust challenges. In *Mayor & City Council of Baltimore v. AbbVie* , 42 F.4th 709 (7th Cir. 2022), the Seventh Circuit[affirmed dismissal](https://media.ca7.uscourts.gov/cgi-bin/rssExec.pl?Path=Y2022%2FD08-01%2FC%3A20-2402%3AJ%3AEasterbrook%3Aaut%3AT%3AfnOp%3AN%3A2911279%3AS%3A0&Submit=Display) of the Sherman Act claims. That case did not adjudicate every patent's validity or establish a but-for date on which each biosimilar would otherwise have launched. The supported conclusion is narrower: the portfolio of settlement/license agreements resolved or managed patent disputes and set contractual U.S. entry dates in 2023.


## FDA approval and commercial launch are different events


FDA approval answers a regulatory question. A settlement license addresses patent rights between the parties. Commercial launch is the manufacturer's market action. One date cannot stand in for another.


Product Original FDA approval First documented U.S. launch Gap


Amjevita September 23, 2016[January 31, 2023](https://www.amgen.com/newsroom/press-releases/2023/01/amjevita-adalimumabatto-first-biosimilar-to-humira-now-available-in-the-united-states) More than six years


Cyltezo August 25, 2017[July 1, 2023](https://www.boehringer-ingelheim.com/us/human-health/skin-and-inflammatory-diseases/biosimilars/cyltezo-first-and-only-fda-approved-interchangeable-biosimilar-humira-now-commercially) Nearly six years


As of September 25, 2026, the[FDA biosimilar list](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/biosimilars/biosimilar-product-information) contains ten approved products referencing Humira. That count is a licensure fact. It does not establish current supply, formulary status, payer coverage, or availability of every presentation.


## How to read the dates without overstating their effect


The FDA describes its publication of the Purple Book patent information as[ministerial](https://purplebooksearch.fda.gov/patent-list) . The reference-product sponsor supplies the patents and corresponding dates. FDA does not decide through publication whether a listed patent is valid, enforceable, infringed, or applicable to a particular biosimilar.


Four boundaries matter:


- A date after 2023 does not prove that the patent currently blocks every biosimilar.
- A 2023 licensed-entry date is not the expiry date for the portfolio.
- As of September 25, 2026, FDA lists orphan exclusivity through February 24, 2028 only for[moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/scripts/opdlisting/oopd/detailedIndex.cfm?cfgridkey=340911) in pediatric patients 5 years of age and older. FDA's protected-indication record adds a limitation: Humira's effectiveness has not been established in patients who lost response to, or were intolerant to, tumor necrosis factor (TNF) blockers. This is not market-wide Humira exclusivity.
- As of September 25, 2026, FDA does not publish a current Humira-wide 12-year reference-product exclusivity date. Reconstructing one would turn an absent field into an unsupported agency determination.


## Scope, method, and legal limits


This U.S. **adalimumab patent landscape** is a public-record map. The patent universe is limited to the 66 sponsor-provided rows on the identified Purple Book page version. The 21 groups use the family IDs displayed by Google Patents as a reproducible supplemental method. Categories describe the titles in each group. They are not claim constructions or opinions on legal effect.


The September 25, 2026 dataset is a dated snapshot, not a live patent-status feed. Its 66 patent numbers and sponsor-provided dates were rechecked against the FDA page on October 5, 2026.


The map does not determine freedom to operate, infringement, validity, enforceability, or whether a settlement license covers a particular product and presentation. A product-specific analysis requires the claims, file wrappers, ownership and terminal-disclaimer records, litigation history, proposed product, and license terms. That is the difference between a public landscape and a product-specific legal opinion.


## Frequently asked questions


### When did Humira's U.S. patent expire?


Humira's basic U.S. patent, US 6,090,382, expired on December 31, 2016. That date does not apply to every Humira-related patent. FDA's sponsor-provided Purple Book list contains other patents with later dates, including dates through 2034.


### Why did Humira biosimilars launch in 2023?


A portfolio of settlement/license agreements set contractual U.S. entry dates in 2023; some of those agreements resolved filed litigation. FDA had approved several products earlier, but approval, a patent license, and commercial launch are separate events.


### Are Humira biosimilars generics?


No. Adalimumab biosimilars are biological products licensed under the biosimilar pathway. Conventional generics are generally small-molecule drugs reviewed under a different statutory and regulatory framework.


### Are there Humira patents after 2023?


Yes. AbbVie's sponsor-provided Purple Book list includes individual patents with dates after 2023 and through November 14, 2034. A listed date does not establish that a patent is valid, enforceable, infringed, applicable to a specific biosimilar, or blocking current entry.


### How many FDA-approved Humira biosimilars are there?


As of September 25, 2026, FDA's list contains ten approved biosimilars referencing Humira. Licensure does not by itself establish present commercial availability, formulary coverage, or availability of every presentation.


### What does interchangeable mean for a Humira biosimilar?


An interchangeable biosimilar meets additional FDA requirements related to pharmacy-level substitution. Depending on state law, a pharmacist may substitute it without consulting the prescriber. The designation does not mean other FDA-approved biosimilars are less safe or effective.
